<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 36 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **52** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `09db1fac87eb082beb83ecd6c565914f0f8062ca` — the merge of head `1704f949d93f62417872e3404349787b41b24390` into base `222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 09db1fac87eb082beb83ecd6c565914f0f8062ca && git checkout 09db1fac87eb082beb83ecd6c565914f0f8062ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378 1704f949d93f62417872e3404349787b41b24390 && git checkout -B drift-repro 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378 && git merge --no-ff 1704f949d93f62417872e3404349787b41b24390

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03a77fb1b670ada66b19e1d37c637274732b2c65`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21197 (body and all eleven comments, among them the ruling 5942811916, the re-claim 5942885323, the amendments 5943017963 and 5943028352, the os-dev-report 5944632767), the #21118 notes 5942902099 and 5943032006, PR #21301 (body, 28-file list, diff — byte-equal to the local `git diff` against merge base `c7396f1a`), tree reads at the head through `git show` / `git grep`, and the head's check-runs read last at 2026-10-02T02:57Z. Classes and positions only; no value is quoted.

### ① Derived judgments

**Ledger mirror (`plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`) — right.** `ledgerView` gains a third limb after the type-keyed mask: every key `collectInternalReadFields(getObjectDef(objectName))` names is deleted. Every side the writer records passes through `ledgerView`: create `new_value` (L1514), both halves of the update diff (L1522–1523), delete `old_value` (L1525), the activity label source (L1585–1586), the milestone and tracked-change views (L1626–1627), and the activity `metadata` old/new (L1691), which reuses the same diff values; the bulk title read skips an `internal` title column (L1177). `getObjectDef` is `engine.getSchema`, the registry the engine's own strip keys on, so a plugin-registered object (`sys_share_link`) is covered — the dogfood pin proves it on a real boot. The "nothing meaningfully changed" skip is judged on the raw diff before the limb, so an internal-only update still writes its row (pinned). Mask-then-omit matches `Engine.maskSecretFields`.

**objectql re-export — right, pure and additive.** Two names added to `core.ts` and `index.ts`, re-exporting the existing `secret-fields.ts` function beside its siblings; no logic, and the `/core` entry already re-exports from that module, so the lean-entry closure is unchanged.

**Census declarations — right, none retyped to `secret`.** Eleven columns across nine objects gain `internal: true` (`sys_api_key.key` and `sys_email.headers_json` already carried it); the plugin-audit pin holds each object's declared set equal to the census. No census object declares a data-door method beyond get/list (`sys_jwks`: none), so no generic write door moves.

**Readback — right where the diff reaches, wrong at one consumer it does not reach.**
- Right: the readback rows in `internal-field-readback.ts` for `sys_jwks.private_key` (absence proves the strip; `required`), `sys_verification.value`, both `sys_two_factor` columns, both SSO blobs and `sys_oauth_application.client_secret`; in `objectql-adapter.ts` the re-attach now runs before `injectClientSecretOnRead` on `findOne` (L909, L918) and `findMany` (L963, L966), the injection parsing the now-internal OIDC blob; `consumeOne` re-attaches before its delete (L1107); the legacy migration recovers `oidc_config` through `recoverInternalFieldsForSystemRead` (`sso-client-secret.ts` L280ff), and the two auth-manager recover sites are `sys_account` only. Engine-level `insert` and `update` results keep the stored row whole (engine L13578 and L15403, the A-prime ruling), so a create or update result handed to better-auth or to a plugin's own route still carries the column; `createLink` returns its local row. `jwt-key-algorithm.ts` reads keys through the adapter's `findMany`, so the jwks row covers it. `sys_sso_provider` is read-only on the data door, so no Setup edit form can blank a blob.
- Wrong — a missed consumer: `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts`, the resolve probe (L170–L205). It reads `password_hash` straight off a generic `engine.find('sys_share_link', …)` to choose between the unknown-token answer and `401 NEEDS_PASSWORD` / `WRONG_PASSWORD`. With the column `internal` that read is always absent, so on this surface every live password-protected link whose redemption failed now answers the unknown-token shape: the password prompt never appears, and a client that asks first cannot open the link. The gate is NOT opened — the service's fail-closed `readShareLinkInternalColumn` holds, and a caller already sending the right password still resolves — but the flow fails. The site's own comment names it the dispatcher twin of the `plugin-sharing` probe this PR fixed and, for cloud's per-environment kernels, the designed primary surface (`registerShareLinkRoutes: false`). Its pin, `domains/share-links-enforcement-context.test.ts` (around L829), drives a `vi.fn` service and engine that hand rows back whole, so it stays green through this — the fake-engine class the dev's own A8 note identified. `packages/runtime` is on no cross-lane declaration.
- Not re-verifiable here: `node_modules` is absent from this checkout, so the dev's trace of the installed better-auth dist (no route reads `verification.identifier` or the OAuth token columns back off a row) rests on the dev's word plus the real-engine pins. The in-repo verifiers are confirmed lookup-only: SCIM reads `active`, `expires_at` and `connection_id` only (`scim-connection-service.ts` L199–230); approvals read `action`, `approver_id` and `request_id` only (`approval-service.ts` L4497ff); `revokeLink` projects without `token`.

**Lookup-only columns — right, with the caveat above.**

**Titles, formulas, highlights — right.** `sys_verification`'s title is a fixed literal and its highlights drop `identifier`; no other census object carries a formula, `titleFormat`, `nameField`, `displayNameField` or `highlightFields` over a now-internal column (all eleven objects read at the head). For the pointer-less objects (`sys_share_link`, both OAuth token objects, `sys_jwks`) the designate-only pass lands on `id`, the first title-eligible field, not on the token column, and the engine synthesizes no title from `nameField` ahead of the strip.

**Pins and A1–A10 — right as claimed, on real engines.** plugin-audit: real `ObjectQL` hooks over an in-memory driver, judged at rest (the subject is the write, not the strip); plugin-auth, plugin-sharing and plugin-approvals: real SQLite engines, plugin-auth with a real `AuthManager` and a key row minted under the pre-change declaration; dogfood: a real showcase boot through built `plugin-audit`. The A1 counts (20 red of 30, the 10 declaration cases green) and A2 (3 of 3) match the suites' shapes; A8's fake-engine discovery was answered with a real-engine second-factor pin. The verification scope stopped at six package suites, eight dogfood files and the derived gate families; the two reds in ③ sit in the remainder the dev declared to CI.

### ② Semver level

- Levels: `minor` for plugin-audit, platform-objects, plugin-auth, plugin-sharing and plugin-approvals under the `!` marker, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at line start — consistent with the repo's breaking-narrowing precedents and `check:no-major`; the `fixed` group moves them together. objectql at `patch` for an added export understates it: in-tree precedent (20312, 20553) writes a new export as a widening at `minor`. Immaterial to the published version under the `fixed` group; wrong as a declaration.
- ADR-0087: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason — the right arm (no authorable key, export or config field is removed or renamed; what narrows is what the generic read path and the ledger return), the same arm as 20166, 20280 and 20546; accepted by `check:adr-0087-registration` per the dev and by `Check Changeset` on this head.
- Prose: carries the signing-key rotation notice and the share-link revoke-and-re-mint notice; does NOT claim the upgrade-time invalidation — it states the lifetime bound of a one-time credential's copy, which is accurate. It is silent that the ruled invalidation is not delivered; that is a residual for ③, not an inaccuracy. The "what changed" list matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Required gates on this head are red (read 2026-10-02T02:57Z). `Dogfood Regression Gate`: failure — shard 2/3, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/two-factor-backup-code-reveal.dogfood.test.ts` (L213–219 reads `sys_two_factor.backup_codes` through `ql.find` and asserts a stored value: a generic-path read of a now-internal column; the product path is pinned green by the plugin-auth real-engine second-factor case). `Test Core (5/6)`: failure — `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/private-credential-row-scope.test.ts` (L263–279 reads `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks` credential columns through `engine.findOne` / `find` on a real engine and expects the value: the same class). `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and the `Test Core` roll-up were still in progress — not yet verdicts. `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`: success. The PR is draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`.
2. The ruled upgrade-time invalidation is not delivered. The refusal came from the dev session's permission layer; it was not routed around, and the unwired module is out of the tree; the PR says `Part of`, not `Fixes`, and the part-of check on this head is green. Landing the mechanism as a part is sound in principle: after it, no new one-time-credential copy reaches the ledger, and the residual is the ledger's existing copies of still-outstanding one-time credentials, admin-readable until each is consumed or expires (minutes to a day by class), beside the pre-upgrade signing-key and share-link copies the notice covers. Whether and how the invalidation half lands is the maintainer's decision; this record designs nothing. The card stays open either way.
3. Cross-lane edits against the #21118 declarations: plugin-auth (`internal-field-readback.ts`, `objectql-adapter.ts`, `sso-client-secret.ts`), plugin-sharing (object, service, routes; the `sharing-service.ts` interface widened in-package) and plugin-approvals (object) match 5942902099 plus 5943032006; the declared `auth-plugin.ts` invalidation wiring was withheld, as reported. `packages/runtime` (① above) is edited by nobody and declared by nobody; the fix needs a declaration on the owning seat before this PR enqueues.
4. The four out-of-scope notes:
   - a formula or title over an `internal` column re-serves it (the read path evaluates formulas before the strip) and no authoring check refuses it: a metadata-authoring trap by Prime Directive #10's definition, so a filed card rather than a note — escalated to the seat;
   - the share-link create route answers its creator with the hash: the plugin's own write response of a creator-chosen password; a note is acceptable, and a `domain:services` card to drop the column from that response is the tidier close — the seat's call;
   - the console's `password_protected` projection is never served: objectui-side, the note stands;
   - the dormant cached rotation-replay response: the note stands; the readback table's comment should name it so enabling the reuse interval does not strip it silently — the seat's call.
5. Other `sys_audit_log` writers outside the mirror (`plugin-audit/src/auth-event-audit.ts`, `plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts`, `service-settings/src/config-change-audit.ts`) write their own event payloads, not object snapshots, and name no census column — no finding, noted for completeness.
